clue.text: One who does for Spooner's mistress

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the syllables in the phrase are swapped, Reverend Spooner style

parts.note: to do for someone is to clean their house, so one who does for is a daily cleaner; that word splits into the syllables DAI and LY for the swap
the second syllable of the word for a daily cleaner, whose opening consonant is swapped with the first syllable's

explanation.surface: A cleaner is muddled up with the lady of the house by the bumbling Reverend Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: DAILY splits as DAI-LY; swapping the opening consonants of the two syllables gives LA-DY. A daily is British slang for a cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mistress of a household is its lady, the woman in charge.

clue.text: Suffer humiliation in encounter by toilets we hear

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side
we hear says the word for toilets is taken as it sounds when spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: loos is British slang for toilets
to face something is to encounter or confront it

explanation.surface: Someone embarrassed by a run-in beside the public conveniences.
explanation.walkthrough: The toilet word comes first in the grid even though 'encounter' comes first in the clue; 'by' only places them side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to lose face is to be humiliated and lose others' respect.

clue.text: On vacation, relative and I get horribly run down

indicators.note: horribly says the letters are wrecked and rearranged
a word on vacation has been emptied, keeping only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker complains that a relative and they get badly worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' empties 'relative' to RE; 'horribly' rearranges RE with ANDIGET.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to run someone down is to belittle or disparage them.

clue.text: Lots of money made from important game?

parts.note: big means important, as in a big decision
bucks are male deer, hunted as game

explanation.surface: A betting man's big win from a major match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' suggests a sporting fixture but it means hunted animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: big bucks is informal for a large sum of money.

clue.text: This month, everything's put in place

parts.note: inst., for instant, is old business shorthand for this month
everything is all

explanation.surface: A report that, as of this month, all is in position.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to set equipment up ready for use is to fix it in place.

clue.text: Unofficial Labour leader splits support

indicators.note: splits says one piece breaks into the middle of the other

parts.note: to back someone is to support them

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A rogue Labour party leader divides the party's backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' suggests the political party or work; only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage: a black market or black economy is unofficial, operating outside legal channels.

clue.text: Feature of church in Asian country

indicators.note: Feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A travel note about an architectural detail of a church in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the People's Republic in East Asia is a country.

clue.text: Plant flag on top of Everest

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: to flag is to tire or droop, to sag

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter of Everest

explanation.surface: A mountaineer plants a flag on the summit of Everest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb about planting the flag; it is the noun, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this grey-leaved herb is a garden plant.

clue.text: Say how one might obtain bass instrument

definitions.text: Say how one might obtain bass instrument

parts.words: Say how one might obtain bass instrument
parts.note: a bass is a fish an angler might catch by throwing a mesh over the water; spoken quickly that phrase names a clicking percussion instrument

explanation.walkthrough: 'bass' and 'instrument' suggest music, but the bass is a fish; casting a net, said quickly, is the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the hand-held clappers used in flamenco are a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Right book to find remedy out

definitions.text: Right book to find remedy out

indicators.note: out says the remedy word lies outside, around the other letters

parts.note: to remedy an ailment is to heal it

explanation.surface: Advice on which book to consult to find a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the right book for finding a remedy is a plant-based guide to cures.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage: as a noun this is a book describing plants and their medicinal uses.

clue.text: Late driver taking this to speed up motion?

definitions.meaning: Ayrton ..., the Brazilian Formula One champion who died in 1994

definitions.text: taking this to speed up motion?
definitions.meaning: a laxative, so it speeds up a bowel motion

explanation.walkthrough: 'speed up' and 'driver' suggest racing; the second sense is the laxative.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a Formula One champion who died racing, and a plant-derived laxative.

clue.text: Doctor Van Helsing taking heroin and getting into bondage?

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged
taking means taking away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Dracula's foe Dr Van Helsing on drugs and into kinky practices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like Van Helsing's title; it is the anagram signal. 'taking' removes the H, leaving VANELSING to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheeky sense: to enslave is to put into bondage, so this is getting people into bondage.

clue.text: Teacher doing time in prison

indicators.note: doing, as in doing without, says a letter is dropped

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher serving a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing time' looks like serving a sentence; here 'doing' removes the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage: schoolchildren address a male teacher by this title.

clue.text: Bundle of cargo about to be unloaded

indicators.note: unloaded says some letters are taken off the cargo word

parts.note: freight is cargo
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A bundle from the ship's cargo is about to be unloaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bundle' looks like a parcel; in slang a bundle is a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a bundle is a scrap or brawl, a punch-up.

clue.text: Need to stop naughty child being a pest

indicators.note: to stop is to plug, so one piece fills a gap in the other

parts.note: a brat is a badly behaved child
lack means need or want

explanation.surface: A naughty child needs to stop being a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pest' reads as the child; it is the definition, a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this rodent, which spread the plague, is a classic household pest.

clue.text: Prior defrocking pious cleric

indicators.note: defrocking strips the pious word away, letter by letter

parts.note: prior means previous, earlier

explanation.surface: A prior stripped of his office, though a devout churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' looks like a monk; it means earlier. The letters of 'pious' are scattered through the word for earlier, so taking them out leaves three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation: the title Reverend, used informally for a clergyman.

clue.text: Designer adopts new means of communication

indicators.note: adopts means takes in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Coco Chanel was a French fashion designer

explanation.surface: A fashion house takes up a new way of getting its message out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a route or medium for passing on information, like a TV station or a contact.

clue.text: See 22
Location-specific numbers are based on a system of rules

indicators.note: in a down clue, based on puts the first piece above the rest

parts.note: a code is a system of rules

explanation.surface: Something is founded on a rule-bound system.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the dialling prefix that identifies a telephone district is a set of digits tied to place.

clue.text: New Yorker perhaps set to become involved in profitable venture

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the other piece

parts.note: a nice little earner is a moneymaking venture

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to join a moneymaking scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' looks like taking part; here it means tangled, so the letters of 'set' are rearranged, and 'in' places them. A nice little earner is British slang for a profitable venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone from New York lives in the eastern United States.

clue.text: Leading actress forgetting start of opening line before great dramatist

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: forgetting says letters are left out

parts.note: Molière, the great French comic playwright

indicators.note: start of takes the first letter of opening

explanation.surface: A star actress drying on the first line before a performance of a classic play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting' removes O (start of 'opening') and L (line) from MOLIERE, leaving MIERE. 'opening' tempts as the definition of a first night.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage: borrowed from French, this word can mean a company's leading lady.

clue.text: Check elements causing trouble in demonstration boiler

definitions.text: Check elements causing trouble in demonstration
definitions.meaning: police containment of protesters by penning them in is called kettling
a kitchen vessel for boiling water

explanation.walkthrough: Kettling is a British police tactic of corralling demonstrators in a confined area.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: penning in unruly protesters, and the appliance for heating water.

clue.text: Duck where roof sticks out and dips?

parts.note: the teal is a small duck
eaves are the overhanging edges of a roof

explanation.surface: A duck sheltering under the overhang ducks and dips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' and 'dips' look like verbs; the first is the bird and the second the definition: tea bags are dipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful: tea is made by dipping tea bags, which hold the dried shredded tea plant.

clue.text: Book brought up author's arousing feelings

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book
the author is the setter, I; author's means I have, shortened

explanation.surface: A writer's book, raised in discussion, stirs emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that stirs strong feelings is emotionally charged.

clue.text: Biker changing gear to steer at regular intervals

indicators.note: changing says the letters are rearranged
at regular intervals takes every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A motorcyclist shifts gear in order to steer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges GEAR to GREA; alternate letters of 'steer' give SER.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a greaser is a leather-clad motorcyclist with slicked-back hair, a rocker.

clue.text: This plot could spell danger

indicators.note: could spell says these letters could be arranged to spell something else

explanation.surface: A sinister plot could mean danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' also means signify, so the surface warns of danger; here it means letters arranged to form a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a plot of land planted with flowers or vegetables.

clue.text: A club rave turned into a shambles

parts.note: a bat is a club used to hit a ball

indicators.note: turned says the word is reversed

parts.note: a riot is a wildly good time, a rave

explanation.surface: A wild party at a club goes badly wrong and ends in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shambles' looks like a mess; its old meaning is a slaughterhouse (the Shambles in York was a street of butchers).
explanation.definitionFit: Old sense: a shambles was originally a meat market or slaughterhouse.

clue.text: Penning article raised money

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bred means raised, as of livestock or children
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Writing a piece raised funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' looks like writing but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: bread is money, as in earning your bread.

clue.text: This could dry up before source of water finally disappears

parts.note: to means before, as in ten to six

indicators.note: finally disappears says the last letter is lost

parts.note: a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: A spring that might run dry before its water runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry up' suggests a source running out; it is drying the dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a cloth used to dry the washing-up can dry up.

clue.text: Master race destroyed elite

indicators.note: destroyed says the letters are broken and rearranged

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: The Nazis' master race destroyed, despite being thought the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges M with RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the cream of anything is its best, the pick of the crop.

clue.text: Intimate sex in modest surroundings doesn't include former partner

indicators.note: surroundings says the modest word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: coy means modestly shy

indicators.note: doesn't include says letters are dropped

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Discreet sex, demurely conducted, leaves the ex out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't include' strips the former partner from 'sex', leaving one letter, which 'surroundings' puts inside the word for modest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small intimate gathering is snug and comfortable.

clue.text: They might play back sound's prime elements

indicators.note: back says the chosen letters are read in reverse
the elements in prime-numbered positions, second, third and fifth, are kept

parts.note: the word sound, with 's for is linking it

explanation.surface: Musicians replaying a recording's main parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters 2, 3 and 5 of SOUND (prime positions) are O, U, D; read back they give the answer. 'play back' looks like replaying a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pair of musicians performing together play a piece.

clue.text: Ended audience's privilege to add new characters to script?

parts.note: over means ended, finished

indicators.note: an audience listens, so the privilege word is taken as heard

parts.note: a right is a privilege or entitlement

explanation.surface: A theatre audience loses its right to rewrite the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Computing sense: to replace stored text by writing new characters over it.

clue.text: Steps taken by desperate fellow in contact with church

indicators.note: in contact with means touching, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: Desperate Dan is the cowboy strongman of the British comic The Dandy
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A man at the end of his tether reaches out to the church for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' looks like measures taken; it means dance steps. Desperate Dan is a British comic-strip character.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sequence of rhythmic steps performed to music.

clue.text: Really taken aback about poem that was sung without a singer

indicators.note: without says the following letter is removed
about says the reversed word wraps around the poem
taken aback says the word Really is read backwards

parts.note: an ode was originally a poem meant to be sung

explanation.surface: Someone startled to learn a poem was sung without a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' reverses 'Really' (YLLAER); the poem goes in after the Y, and 'without' then removes the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Alpine singer warbling between chest voice and falsetto is a singer.

clue.text: Supporter's run on board plane?

indicators.note: on board means inside, so the letter goes into the other piece

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball; the 's means has
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A backer is running to catch a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft; it is the plane tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the London plane is a tall broad-leaved tree.
